Dictation lands on the screen you are looking at and keeps the words you said last, and the live intelligence board can be told to stop refreshing itself.

## The board stops when you tell it to

While a meeting records, the intelligence board re-reads the whole transcript every 30 seconds. Over a long call that adds up, and there was no way to pause it short of dropping back to a general meeting and giving up the board entirely.

- A pause button now sits next to re-extract in the board header. Stop it and nothing runs on its own — the re-extract button stays as the manual trigger.
- The choice sticks, so a board you stopped stays stopped across meetings and launches.
- On general meetings the same button stops the agenda checklist's automatic check.

## Voice typing

- The floating overlay opens on the display your cursor is on. On any Retina Mac it had been landing on whichever screen the main window happened to be on, for most of the screen area.
- Letting go of the dictation key no longer cuts off the end of what you said. Audio recorded just before the release could be discarded along with it, and the busier the app was — right after a meeting, say — the more went missing.
